paragraphs.source_en: On the road from Hakone to Odawara, Masanobu Takekoshi and Naotsugu Andō kept pondering the question Tokugawa Ieyasu had posed. Whenever Ieyasu put a question to them, they would wrestle with it until they reached a firm conclusion. Ieyasu, too, seemed to find this rather amusing and would occasionally devise some peculiar question to throw at them. This time, however, even as they neared Bell Forest, the gateway to Edo, Ieyasu had said nothing more about Mount Fuji.
